thread:
maria: Quick follow-up on continuous-batching tradeoffs — we need a concrete deprecation/migration plan for the old `enqueue()` admission surface. The runtime-latency teams keep hitting opaque headroom regressions when customers opt into prefix sharding.

kevin: Agreed. The old `enqueue()` has too many knobs embedded. Is the plan to replace it with `admit_v2()` (explicit hints + shard_id) and then funnel telemetry through that?

maria: That's the idea. `admit_v2()` would take `{prefix_hint, shard_key?, deadline_ms?}` and the scheduler would be able to make deterministic shard placement + KV cache accounting. That should make headroom accounting reliable.

alex: Two concerns: 1) backwards compatibility for SDKs, 2) how this interacts with quantized models where token fanout changes memory footprint. We need a safe fallback for customers who can't upgrade SDKs.

sam: For quantization: we could surface an extra cost_hint in `admit_v2()` (e.g. `kv_weight`/`compute_weight`) so the kernel selection can pre-reserve buffers. It's coarse but better than current blind admission.

maria: Good call. So fields: `prefix_hint` (string), `shard_key` (optional string), `deadline_ms` (optional), `cost_hint` (enum: LIGHT/MEDIUM/HEAVY). Default MEDIUM.

kevin: How do we route older calls? Option A: compatibility proxy that translates `enqueue()` into `admit_v2()` with defaults. Option B: deprecate immediately and rely on telemetry + migration guides. I'd prefer A for a gradual roll.

maria: We should do A for Hosted and Dedicated, but for Private we need a feature flag since some customers want to keep runtime-legacy behavior.

alex: Observability gap: current dashboards don't show per-shard KV hit/miss or per-admit cost attribution. We'll need a new telemetry schema: `admit_id`, `shard_id`, `cost_hint`, `latency_ms`, `evicted:boolean`. Without that we can't debug headroom regression.

sam: I sketched a prometheus + trace proto. We should emit an event on admit decision and on batch cut. Minimal metrics: `redwood_admit_decisions_total{result="admitted|rejected|evicted"}`, `redwood_admit_latency_ms_bucket`, and spans with `admit_id`/`shard_id`.

maria: Nice. Add `kv_cache_reserved_bytes` sample per admit to tie to memory pressure.

kevin: Operationally, pre-reserving on admit means we may underutilize memory if we over/under-estimate cost_hint. Need hysteresis: allow optimistic admit but evict low-priority entries when pressure hits X%. Also an eviction score that considers `prefix_hint` locality.

alex: Eviction score should avoid evicting entries that are hot for the same shard. So track per-shard recency. Also consider a fast-path to reconstitute prefix cache for small prefixes to avoid expensive cold-starts.

sam: For rollout strategy: 1) add `admit_v2()` in runtime and SDK, proxy translation for old `enqueue()` with `cost_hint=MEDIUM` (hosted & dedicated only). 2) Add telemetry emitted by admit decisions and batch-cuts. 3) Run canary with 5% traffic, measure headroom/regressions and KV eviction deltas. 4) Expose feature flag for Private customers to opt-in.

kevin: What about API compatibility in console and rollouts? We should add a per-tenant config `admit_mode: legacy|compat|strict` with defaults `compat`. This allows gradual tightening.

maria: Agree. Also include an auto-suggest to customers in console when telemetry shows >20% eviction increase post-admit, recommending `cost_hint=HEAVY` or explicit shard_key.

alex: Tests: unit for admit-to-shard mapping, integration for end-to-end KV reuse across admit+batch-cut, and chaos test where we simulate quantized-model memory footprint doubling mid-batch.

maria: Let's also update runbooks: if `redwood_admit_decisions_total{result="evicted"}` spikes, runbook step 2 should query per-shard `kv_cache_reserved_bytes` and fallback to `compat` mode.

kevin: One more thing: we need to document the deprecation timeline publicly. Proposal: 90-day feature-flag-only compat, 60-day soft-deprecation (warning in SDK), 90-day hard deprecation after no major regressions.

sam: Sounds reasonable. I'll draft RFC follow-up with the fields, metrics, and canary checklist.

maria: Thanks. Action items: @kevin add proxy impl + config flag, @sam draft telemetry proto and canary playbook, @alex add eviction scoring sketch and tests. I'll circle back with rollout timing. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: CI pipeline — integration tests for `admit_v2()` landed on branch `runtime/admit-v2` (build 482). All unit tests green, a couple flaky infra tests marked flaky.

kevin: cool — i'll pick up the proxy PR and wire feature flag.

alex: I'll start the eviction scoring prototype and add perf tests.

sam: RFC follow-up in docs/ incoming — will ping when ready.

maria: Great thread. We'll follow up in the RFC doc and sync next week.
